notes:
Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for high-throughput embeddings + low-latency chat reranking. Primary ask: guaranteed sustained throughput 600k tokens/min, P99 latency <=150ms for 256-token responses, burst to 1.2M tokens/min for 20min spikes, predictable unit economics across commit tiers.

Timeline:
- 2024-10-28: Intro call (AE: Ethan) — customer said "need predictable monthly cost vs spot."
- 2024-11-04: SE deep dive (Priya) — covered perf targets and model mix: quantized 13B for embeddings, licensed medium chat model for assistant.
- 2024-11-15: Security review kickoff — NDA signed, security FAQ shared (drive link).
- 2024-11-29: Perf POC started (baseline on 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs): observed ~18k tokens/sec aggregate for embeddings; chat baseline 220 req/s for 256-token responses with avg latency 120ms; KV cache hit ratio ~42%.
- 2024-12-05: Cost modeling workshop w/ finance — sensitivity table built for commit levels (4,8,12 GPUs) and utilization (35%, 60%, 80%).
- 2024-12-12: SLA negotiation call — customer pushing for 99.95% uptime + 10% credits for missed SLOs; Redwood proposed 99.9% + enhanced monitoring and faster incident triage.

Use-case details:
- Workloads: nightly high-throughput embedding batch jobs (semantic index refresh) + daytime interactive chat/rerank for customer-facing assistant (latency-sensitive).
- Traffic pattern: diurnal with two daytime spikes; reserved capacity must cover daytime SLOs, batch can be scheduled to off-peak or run on burst/spot.
- Model pathing: primary quantized open models for embeddings, proprietary fine-tuned chat for customer messages; fallback to trimmed model when capacity constrained.

Cost modeling highlights:
- Assumptions: token mix 60% embedding tokens (batch), 40% chat tokens (interactive); avg chat response length ~220 tokens; embeddings billed per vector generation token.
- Throughput mapping: 1 x A100-equivalent GPU ~4.5k chat tokens/sec under quantized 13B w/ efficient batching; embeddings throughput ~55k vectors/hr per GPU depending on batch sizing.
- Commit scenarios: 4 GPUs (starter), 8 GPUs (recommended for steady-state SLOs), 12 GPUs (headroom + future growth). At 60% utilization, 8 GPUs keeps P99 latency comfortably under SLO and reduces unit cost ~22% vs 4 GPUs.
- Unit economics: with reserved discount, blended cost per 1k tokens estimated $0.0055 at 8 GPUs and $0.0078 at 4 GPUs; at 12 GPUs and 80% utilization unit cost could be ~$0.0038. Utilization sensitivity: dropping to 35% increases per-1k-token cost by ~65%.
- Burst behavior: proposed design includes scheduled burst pool (contracted burst) for predictable short spikes; customer wants formal guarantee for 2x sustained burst for 20 minutes without impacting committed SLOs.
- SLA negotiation points: uptime target, maintenance windows (requested narrow window 02:00-04:00 local), service credits threshold (customer asks credits for unscheduled downtime >5min), and measurable latency SLOs at token lengths 64/256/1024.

Outstanding technical questions:
- Validate KV cache sizing per tenant and expected hit ratio (assumed 40-50%).
- Confirm network egress/residency accounting for cross-region fallback.
- Can Redwood guarantee burst capacity without oversubscription to other enterprise pools? Need explicit burst policy behavior.

Next steps:
- Deliver updated cost workbook with per-token lookup table and three commit proposals (4/8/12 GPUs) by 2024-12-20.
- Schedule SLA redline call with legal + procurement 2024-12-22.
